interface.signature: def maxScoreWords(words: List[str], letters: List[str], score: List[int]) -> int:

preconditions.description: Each word in the input list has a length of at most 15 characters.
Each element in the letters list is a single lowercase English letter.
The score list contains exactly 26 integers, one for each lowercase English letter.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= s <= 10 for s in score)
preconditions.description: Each score in the score list is between 0 and 10 (inclusive).
All letters in the letters list are lowercase English letters.

preconditions.expression: all('a' <= c <= 'z' for word in words for c in word)
preconditions.description: All characters in all words are lowercase English letters.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= score[i] <= 10 for i in range(26))
postconditions.description: The score list remains unchanged (implicitly, since it is an input).

postconditions.expression: any(return_value == sum(score[ord(c) - ord('a')] for word in selected_words for c in word) for selected_words in combinations(words, k) for k in range(len(words) + 1))
postconditions.description: The returned score is the maximum possible score achievable by selecting a subset of words (each used at most once) that can be formed using the given letters, where each letter in the letters list can be used at most once across all selected words.

postconditions.expression: all(len(word) <= len(letters) for word in words)
postconditions.description: The length of each word is at most the length of the letters list (implicitly, since words can only be formed if their letters are a subset of the given letters).
